title: Accidental Discharge of Licensed Weapon at Varanasi Airport
body_text:
On 16 August 2026, at approximately 0930 hours, a passenger, namely Shri Kamlesh Kedarnath Rai, scheduled to travel from Varanasi to Mumbai on Air India Express flight IX 1810 declared a licensed firearm (7.62 mm pistol with 21 live cartridges) at the check-in counter, as required under the prescribed procedure.
The passenger was escorted to the designated screening area for completion of the mandatory security formalities. During the handling and inspection of the weapon, a round was accidentally discharged. The projectile ricocheted and caused injuries to two screening personnel, Shri Rohit Raj and Ms Suman Kumari.
Both personnel were immediately provided assistance and shifted to New Lakshmi Trauma Center, Varanasi, for medical treatment.
The local police were informed immediately and the passenger has been detained for investigation and further action in accordance with law.
The Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS) is examining the circumstances leading to the incident, including adherence to the prescribed procedures for handling and carriage of licensed weapons at airports. Appropriate action will be taken based on the findings.
The incident was promptly contained and airport operations are continuing without disruption.
*****
Divyanshu Kumar

enrichment.summary: On 16 August 2026, during mandatory security screening at Varanasi airport, a licensed firearm declared by a passenger traveling on Air India Express flight IX 1810 accidentally discharged, injuring two CISF/security screening personnel who were shifted for medical treatment. The passenger was detained by police, and the Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS) is examining lapses in weapon-handling procedures.
enrichment.context:
Airports in India follow a standard procedure for passengers carrying licensed firearms: the weapon must be declared at check-in, unloaded, and handled separately by security personnel for verification before being stowed in the aircraft hold. BCAS, under the Ministry of Civil Aviation, is the regulatory body responsible for laying down and enforcing aviation security protocols, including those for carriage of firearms and ammunition. Incidents like this typically trigger a review of standard operating procedures (SOPs) at the specific airport and sometimes lead to tightening of national guidelines on firearm handling by screening staff.

While isolated security lapses of this kind occasionally occur, they rarely lead to systemic policy changes unless a pattern emerges or a BCAS inquiry recommends structural reforms. This release documents an operational incident and BCAS's ongoing examination, without announcing any new policy, rule change, or systemic finding.
